title: Daylight or Disappear
paragraphs: Julian found Maya on the promenade twenty minutes after Ethan walked away with dignity. Twenty minutes was long enough for the offer to finish forming.

She stood at the rail like someone unstitched. Dress still formal-adjacent. Ring on. The whole-face laugh from the floor still ghosting her mouth. He stopped a careful distance away — no claim, no chase — and waited until she looked at him. Own the floor first. Then the only clean options left: daylight, or disappear.

"I own my part," he said first, spare. "I crossed that floor. Hand at your waist in front of him. I didn't refuse you when you asked in public. That's on me. I won't rewrite myself as pulled helplessly. I chose."
Maya's laugh broke wrong. "I asked with my body in front of a room. Ethan went still. Did you see his face?"
"I saw." Julian's jaw flexed. No victory. "He deserved better than learning it from our feet."
Wind moved between them. Ship lights. Night 7 pressing toward Miami already in the hull's vibration. When he spoke the offer, mid-twenties rust lived under it without needing a speech about rules.

"I can disappear," he said quietly. "Rest of the cruise. After. So you can choose without me in every corridor. Or I stay if you ask in daylight — meaning you tell him, or you put telling him on a real timeline. Not a forever-secret in Charlotte while March goes on like theater. Keeping me *and* the dark isn't on the table. Cabana terms still stand. The floor just made the cost visible."
Maya's hands gripped the rail. "You're asking me to blow up my life to keep you."

"I'm asking you not to keep me *and* the dark." Exact. Kind without soft-focus. "Different ask. If you need me gone to face him, say so. I'll go to 7203 and stay gone. If you want me after honesty, ask in daylight. I only come back if you choose free. No chase."

The demand rose between them like weather. Maya couldn't ask him to stay *and* keep Ethan in the dark. Her mouth opened on a plea and closed on a panic. "I need — I can't — not tonight's sentences. His face. Gloria. The deposit. I need air that isn't you."
"Okay." Cost in the word. He stepped back. Hands empty. "Take the air. I'm not following you to 8145. I'm not texting. Offer stays on the table until you push it off."
She looked at him like she wanted to climb into the offer and set it on fire at once. Then she turned and walked — isolation path toward dark moment already opening under her feet.
Julian stayed at the rail until she was gone. Owned his part. Offered daylight or disappear. Did not chase.
He went to Compass & Low. Mara set down water without commentary, hard look softened a fraction into something like respect for a man not performing chase.
"You look like someone who told the truth and didn't get a parade," Mara said.
"Truth isn't a parade route." Julian drank. "If she asks me gone, I'm gone. If she asks in daylight later, that's different. I'm not hunting her through decks tonight."
Mara nodded once. "Ship docks tomorrow. Land is colder. Remember that before you invent ship solutions."
"No ship solutions," Julian said, and meant no bubble ending, and left a tip, and returned to 7203.

He sat in the dark with Ethan's stillness replaying and Maya's wrong laugh and the knowledge that the loneliest beat now belonged to her alone — and that respecting it was the only clean move left on a ship that hid secrets badly and had just stopped hiding theirs. Note draft already forming for pre-dawn if she pushed him away into duty costume: respect the ask; no chase; terms stand; daylight if she asked later, or gone. Phone face-down. Offer on the table. Hands empty on purpose.
